top.title: Russell vents fury at Mercedes after missing out on pole in São Paulo
top.description: FILE PHOTO - British formula One driver George Russell of team Mercedes speaks to the media at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, ahead of the Mexican Formula One Grand Prix. (is associated with: «Russell vents fury at Mercedes after missing out on pole in São Paulo») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa George Russell was again left furious with his Mercedes team after being pipped to pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix by Lando Norris. Norris, deposed as world champion by Kimi Antonelli last weekend, conquered thunderstorms to clinch an impressive pole as the rain poured down. Russell was facing a five-place grid penalty due to an engine change but was still determined to land pole as he and Norris slugged it out. But he was told to back off on his final flying lap before the rain worsened and his chance had gone. "You told me to back off, what the hell?" Russell bellowed on the radio. Team principal Toto Wolff tried to calm his driver by saying: "George, you are p2." That seemed to make matters worse, as Russell barked: "P2? I don't want to be P2, I want to be P1!" It adds to a season of frustration for pre-season title favourite Russell, having had to watch 20-year-old team-mate Antonelli storm to the title while he says he had been undone by issues in 14 of the 20 weekends prior to this. "Congrats to Lando but that was a pole lap and a misjudgement on our side," Russell said. "For me personally, given the circumstances of last week, it would have meant a lot to me to take pole today. "I missed it last week by nine milliseconds, but that was a real surprise. Today I really felt every lap I was doing was... I was at the top of the leaderboard most laps I completed. "So yeah, I'm really disappointed with how that panned out. In the scheme of things, it doesn't change a huge amount." Russell was asked about the message from Wolff but played down any frustration over it. "When you're a driver, you're the one who feels it the most," he added. "You've got to remember, we collectively made a misjudgement today. And there's members of my team who are going to be feeling as bad as I am currently. So it's important to remember that and we need to just keep the morale high. "There's no point for pole, but it would have just been a nice little one to add to the tally." Wolff admitted in a video posted by Mercedes they may have made the wrong call with Russell behind Alex Albon on track, saying: "George was absolutely the quickest and should have been on pole. We are trying to do our best, I'm not sure we should have aborted the lap." Russell will start seventh, one of a number of drivers hit by grid drops. Lewis Hamilton received a 10-place penalty but his new engine began smoking during practice and Ferrari ultimately had to change his entire power unit. He will start from the back alongside Max Verstappen, while Charles Leclerc starts 14th after his 10-place drop. top.title: Dominant wins for Corning, Horseheads, TAE, Waverly in football semis
top.description: Corning, Horseheads, Waverly, and Thomas A. Edison were dominant in Section 4 football semifinal contests, earning spots in championship games next week. Watkins Glen/Odessa-Montour fell short against defending state champion Tioga Central in a Class D semifinal. A recap of Elmira-Corning region teams in sectional semifinals played Friday, Nov. 6 and Saturday, Nov. 7. Class AA: Corning 43, Ithaca 14 Hours after it was announced he was named the section's Class AA Player of the Year by the Section 4 Football Coaches Association , Corning's John Graham returned the opening kickoff 85 yards for a touchdown to set the tone in the Hawks' home semifinal triumph Friday night. "When we're clicking on all three sides of the ball, we're pretty good and we're tough to beat," Corning head coach Mike Johnston Jr. said. "To open the game up with the kickoff return was huge. He shows why he's the Section 4 Class AA Player of the Year and continues to make big plays for us." Graham added touchdown runs of 5 yards and 1 yard as Corning led 30-7 at halftime on the way to its second lopsided win this season against the Little Red. Corning, which began its combined program in 2010, has never lost to Ithaca. Graham finished with 96 yards on 13 rushes on a night Corning had 10 players run the ball. Fellow wingback Keegan Kelly added 86 yards on eight rushes to go with an interception on defense. Fullback Keegan VanCise carried 14 times for 78 yards, including a 1-yard touchdown. Ashton Neally added two touchdowns for the Hawks, the first on a 19-yard reception of a Nate Bretch throw, and the second on a 4-yard run that put Corning up, 44-7, just over two minutes into the final quarter. "It wasn't like somebody ran for 200 yards," Johnston said. "It was a collective effort by our team. A lot of the credit goes to our line. We were able to throw the ball tonight as well, and our defense was pretty solid as well. Just an all-around great effort by everybody." Touchdowns for Ithaca (5-5) came on a 36-yard run from Jasmir Robbins in the first half, and a 29-yard strike from Leo Fiorello to Shy'von Williams late in the game. Robbins rushed for 72 yards on eight carries. He sat out the second half after he was shaken up on the final play of the first half. Corning responded after a 33-7 loss to Union-Endicott in last week's regular-season finale. Little went right for the Hawks in that game, including more than 200 penalty yards, a dropped touchdown, and some injuries that sidelined key players in the second half. "I'd like to think that we turned the corner," Johnston said. "We've still got a ways to go with some guys, getting them healthy. I know Elmira gets the bye week and their kids will be back to full go." Up next : Corning (6-4) will play Elmira (6-3) in the championship game at 6 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13 at Elmira's Thomas J. Hurley Athletic Complex. Elmira topped Corning, 14-8, in the regular season and has beaten the Hawks in the last three Section 4 Class AA finals.

top.title: Billam-Smith stopped as Clarke repeats amateur win
top.description: Chev Clarke (left) had previously beaten Chris Billam-Smith in a three-round amateur contest [Getty Images] Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith was knocked down and stopped for the first time in his career as Chev Clarke won their all-British non-title fight on Saturday. Londoner Clarke landed a big right hand at the start of the seventh round and although Billam-Smith beat the count, he was down again moments later after a barrage of punches. The contest was allowed to continue but the Bournemouth fighter looked unsteady on his legs and when Clarke connected with two more blows, the referee stepped in. Billam-Smith immediately protested against the decision, while Clarke stood in the middle of the ring shrugging his shoulders. Clarke moves to 13 wins with two defeats and inflicts the third professional defeat for Billam-Smith who also lost to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and Richard Riakporhe in 2019. "I do what champions do," said Clarke, who also beat Billam-Smith when they met in the amateur ranks a decade ago. "I'm happy. Arsenal won and I won. My training camp was good and you saw that in the ring. I'll take all-comers going forward." The likes of heavyweight Johnny Fisher, Traitors star King Kenny and strongman Eddie Hall were all spotted watching on from ringside in a Copper Box arena that was far from full, with just the lower tier of seats open for fans. After a slow start to the contest with lots of holding, Clarke looked the sharper man as he landed some clean shots on the former world champion. In the second round, the Londoner landed a big overhand right to the side of Billam-Smith's head. Clarke also connected in the third round with a big uppercut and an overhand right that snapped back Billam-Smith's head. The former world champion, struggling to find his rhythm, was caught by another uppercut before Billam-Smith responded with a short right hook that made Clarke stumble back to his corner. But in the seventh round Clarke broke Billam-Smith down, scoring two quick knockdowns before the referee intervened. Fight promoter Dana White said after the fight that he felt the decision to stop the fight might have been a little premature. top.title: Big Ten Network cuts to analyst Mike Locksley following Maryland’s win over Purdue
top.description: Credit: BTN A little over two weeks ago, Mike Locksley stood on the Maryland Terrapins’ sidelines as their head football coach. On Saturday, he sat in the Big Ten Network studio watching them snap a 13-game Big Ten losing streak against the Purdue Boilermakers. The Terps held on to defeat the Boilermakers 34-29 in West Lafayette, Indiana, and afterward interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim received a Gatorade bath and was carried off the field, creating a heartwarming scene. That scene got a little awkward when BTN left the game and returned to its studio show, where Locksley, fired Oct. 21 after eight seasons , was asked to comment on the victory and celebration. The former coach was graceful, praising the team and Aazaar, and noting that he’d picked them to win the game beforehand. “Congrats to Coach Aazaar and the Maryland Terrapin football team. It was a complimentary game,” he said. “When you look in the first half, the way the defense did a great job of holding them to field goals, and then the offense comes out, four TDs in four straight drives to blow the game open and then win it at the end in a close game at the end.” Fellow BTN analyst Gerry DiNardo seemed to understand the uncomfortable nature of the moment, and took a moment to point out that quarterback Malik Washington, who passed for 253 yards and was responsible for four touchdowns, was Locksley’s recruit. “Malik Washington’s not at Maryland if it wasn’t for you,” said DiNardo, patting his fellow analyst’s arm. “I appreciate that,” replied Locksley. top.title: 5 major takeaways from Penn State’s nail-biting win over Washington
top.description: It feels like Penn State has finally regained control over its season. After a four-game losing streak that followed a 3-0 start to the season, the blue and white have won two in a row, and it looks like they truly belong in the Big Ten. The Nittany Lions took on Washington on Saturday afternoon, and they won 28-25 in what was almost a mirror image of the Wisconsin game earlier in the season. The offense moved the ball and scored at will in the first half, while the defense put a familiar beatdown on the Huskies ’ offense. But then the offense went cold in the final two quarters, and the defense softened up and allowed the Huskies back in the game. However, Penn State was able to salt away the game in the end, and it escaped Washington with a win. Here are five of the biggest takeaways from the team’s second conference win of the season. We belong For a while there, it looked like head coach Matt Campbell and his gang of Iowa State transfers were no match for the Big Ten. They lost their first four games in the conference, and they were getting out-coached and outplayed for much of that time. But after back-to-back wins, with those Cyclones players being the focal points, their viability in the conference is no longer in question. There may not be much to accomplish for the team this season, but this is solid groundwork for the development of the program going forward. Beggars can’t be choosers Washington might not be the cream of the crop in the Big Ten, but they are certainly a good team. Penn State’s fans have been starving for a win against a team that has some life, and they finally got it this week. If may not have been the prettiest game, and the Nittany Lions may have avoided a catastrophe at the end of the game, but a win is a win. A victory was what everyone wanted, so we can’t complain about the path it took to get here. Competition It looked like Koby Howard was Penn State’s clear-cut best wide receiver when the season began. Now that he’s been out of action for more than two months, we’re finding out that it may not be the case. Wide receiver Chase Sowell has thrived in Howard’s absence, and he had the best game of his career by far on Saturday. He finished the contest with four catches for 125 yards and a touchdown, and he had a number of highlight plays that made him look like a star. Not only is it looking like the Nittany Lions have two No. 1 receivers, but they might both be stars as well. Rookie wall Linebacker Josiah Zayas struggled mightily for the first time all season. The true freshman got juked out on the very first play from scrimmage, and it set the table for the rest of the game. The Huskies tried to make a late push, and on the touchdown they scored to make the game 28-17, Zayas seemed confused about what he was supposed to be doing in coverage. He then gave up another touchdown on a fourth-quarter drive where he slipped. He looks like he has a bright future on this team, but Saturday’s game was not a good one for him

top.title: Oregon's Teitum Tuioti exits Ohio State game with injury. What we know
top.description: COLUMBUS, Ohio – Oregon pulled off the upset Nov. 7 with a 41-28 win against Ohio State. But the victory could've also come with a costly injury for the Ducks . Starting outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti injured his left knee in the fourth quarter and was wearing a brace as he was carted to the locker room when the game ended. Teitum Tuioti injury: How it happened Tuioti's injury came on a fourth-and-13 pass rush with 9:16 to play as his leg buckled when he was attempting to spin out of a block. The senior was down on the field for a few minutes and needed help getting to the sideline. Tuioti had two tackles in the game, including one for a loss of yards. He also played a key role in one of the Ducks' most impactful plays when he took a direct snap with Oregon in punt formation and threw a 30-yard pass to fellow outside linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei for a first down. LOS ANGELES – Since JJ Redick took the helm as head coach of the Los Angeles Lakers , the team has used their two-way contract players quite often. In year one, Christian Koloko and Trey Jemison received plenty of minutes amid the Anthony Davis trade, while Jordan Goodwin had his deal converted to standard contract. Last year, Drew Timme and Nick Smith Jr. contributed to wins while Smith had his contract converted. This year, one player looking to potentially get minutes for the Lakers is Chris Mañon . The second-year guard is back on a two-way contract, and during his rookie season, Redick mentioned that he has the tools to become an elite defensive player in the NBA . Chris Mañon didn’t see much playing time last year with the Lakers, and he’s beginning this season getting reps in the G League with the rebranded Coachella Valley Lakers. While Mañon has always been more of a shooting guard, one thing the Lakers’ coaching staff had asked of him during training camp and the preseason was to play more point guard. You got to help them out all while handling pressure, people trying to take the ball from you,” Mañon said during Coachella Valley Media Day on Nov. 2. “It’s super fun for me. I love learning new things and being able to be versatile, so it’s been super fun.” Across the last two seasons, Mañon has appeared in a total of 11 games for the Lakers. He averaged 11.6 points, 6.0 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.1 steals while shooting 51.2 percent from the field. While he has the most experience out of the Lakers’ three two-way contract players, it’s a good bet he’ll see most of his game reps with Coachella Valley. top.description: MADISON, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 07: Ryan Hopkins #10 of the Wisconsin Badgers takes off running in the second quarter against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Camp Randall Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers blew out the Rutgers Scarlet Knights 31-10 on Saturday, earning bowl eligibility for the first time in three years as they improved to 6-2 on the season. True freshman Ryan Hopkins got his first career start, while the Badgers had another offensive line change. Still, they got out ahead early and finished the game strong en route to a blowout. Here are three quick takeaways from Wisconsin’s win over Rutgers. Hopkins has his moments For one of the first times this season, we saw the Badgers passing attack see some life. Yes, it was against a poor Rutgers team that didn’t have much pressure, but Hopkins looked fairly confident in the pocket and the Badgers let him rip. Hopkins made a number of good plays, as well as a few he would want back that didn’t end up hurting the Badgers. But he looked the part as a true freshman. He was very efficient throwing the ball, looked to target all parts of the field, and made throws that Colton Joseph hadn’t made. Wisconsin now gets a trial period with Hopkins over the next three games to assess where he’s at ahead of the 2027 season. But it was a very positive look in his first start. Pressuring the quarterback The Badgers came to play defensively, and a big part of it was getting after the quarterback. Wisconsin had five sacks, with Sebastian Cheeks, Nicolas Clayton, Charles Perkins, Nolan Vils, and Junior Poyser all getting sacks. They were able to pressure AJ Surace quite a bit, and stopping the run helped them get into third down situations, where they held Rutgers to 4 of 13 on third downs. It was a better day after Wisconsin couldn’t disrupt the quarterback against Iowa, with Hank Brown completing 20 of 24 passes for 222 yards. Good day for the boys up front. Bowl eligible It should be the expectation, but Wisconsin has returned to bowl eligibility after two disappointing years. It was a good bounce back for the Badgers, who were embarrassed last weekend, as they dominated Rutgers for much of this one. Now, the focus should be on Wisconsin winning at least two or the next three to take advantage of their favorable schedule. Going forward, the focus needs to be on Ryan Hopkins’s development and continued improvement of the offense, while Wisconsin’s defense remains to be aggressive. With how Wisconsin looked on Saturday, it feels like they must win that season-ender against Minnesota to cap off a successful season. But they had a strong performance Saturday and reached a key milestone.

top.title: Rutgers Offense Stalls in Second Half, Falls to Wisconsin 31 to 10
top.description: MADISON, WI - NOVEMBER 07: Rutgers Scarlet Knights quarterback AJ Surace (10) throws a pass in a college football game between the Rutgers Scarlet Knights and the Wisconsin Badgers on November 7th, 2026 at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, WI. (Photo by Dan Sanger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Rutgers football fell to Wisconsin 31 to 10 in a game where a three-point halftime deficit turned into a rout by the game’s end. In the final 30 minutes of play, the Scarlet Knights would be held scoreless while the Badgers found the momentum offensively to pull away. Rutgers would keep it close throughout the first half, as they only found themselves down by three at halftime. The Knights would force the Badgers to punt twice and would twice strand the Badgers on fourth down deep in their own territory twice, forcing them to take two field goals. Rutgers would keep pace by scoring a touchdown of their own, off of a 30-yard touchdown pass to freshman wide receiver Dyzier Carter, and by hitting a 45-yard field goal. The field goal was kicked by Jack Scullion, with starting kicker Dane Pizarro out due to injury. Wisconsin’s offense would start humming in the second half, with the Knights having no answer for it. The Badgers would kick a field goal on their first drive of the half to extend their lead before scoring two touchdowns on their next two drives. Rutgers’ defense would recover a fumble on Wisconsin’s fourth drive of the half, but their offense would be unable to score for the entire half as the Badgers would cruise to victory. The Knights’ defense continued the tradition of making backup freshman quarterbacks look like battle-tested veterans, as they allowed Ryan Hopkins to complete 18 out of 24 passes for 241 yards and three touchdowns. On the ground, Wisconsin ran the ball 29 times for 122 yards. On offense, the Knights struggled to keep their quarterback upright, as they surrendered five total sacks on the day and eight total tackles for loss. They also struggled to get the run going, totaling 94 yards on 36 carries, or 2.6 yards per carry. The one slight positive in this game is that AJ Surace looked more consistent in this game than in games past. He completed 14 out of 24 total passes for 161 yards, one touchdown, and no interceptions. This game was a step in the right direction for Surace, compared to his performance in games past. Rutgers will hope to get a few of their playmakers back healthy for next week, as they will return home to play the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Saturday, Nov. 14. That game will take place at 12:30 p.m. and will be broadcast live on the Big Ten Network.

top.title: Could Yankees’ Ben Rice return to catcher in 2027?

Ben Rice made his MLB debut with the New York Yankees during the 2024 season. He primarily played first base, but did catch in one contest. The 2025 campaign saw Rice spend various amounts of time in different roles. He played first base and designated hitter most of the time, but he did catch in 36 games (26 starts). In his 2026 All-Star season , Rice did not catch a single game . With New York in need of catching help, could Rice return to the position in 2027? Bryan Hoch of MLB.com recently published an article that looked at areas of the lineup where the Yankees can improve this offseason. Unsurprisingly, catcher was mentioned. Hoch brought up the idea of Rice being a potential “in-house” option for New York. “One in-house alternative to consider is Rice,” Hoch wrote. “… Given their roster construction, the Yankees would benefit from keeping Rice’s catching in play.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The chances of Ben Rice becoming a full-time catcher in the big leagues are likely slim. He just hit 41 home runs and recorded an .897 OPS while spending time at DH and first base. Forcing Rice to consistently focus on catcher could impact his offensive performance. However, Hoch makes a good point. “Keeping Rice’s catching in play” makes sense. Even if he catches just 20-30 games, having him be a third option of sorts at the position makes sense. The Yankees could lean on two catchers — likely a starter and a backup unless a quality platoon opportunity presents itself. Rice could then start on occasion while still serving as the DH or first baseman most of the time. Will the Yankees take that approach? It remains to be seen. If the Yankees want an uptick in offensive production at the catcher position, 30 games of Rice catching would go a long way toward helping that goal become a reality. All of that might help you sleep at night — but it doesn’t change the end result. nigeria.title: A Ballot on a Burial Date? Northern Nigeria Confronts the Symbolism of January 16
nigeria.description: By Hassan A Karofi The choice of dates in politics is often presented as a matter of administrative convenience. Yet history teaches us that dates carry powerful symbolism, especially in societies where collective memories of tragedy and triumph remain deeply rooted. As Nigeria prepares for a presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2026, it is important to reflect on what that date means to millions of people, particularly in Northern Nigeria, where January 16 is associated with one of the darkest episodes in the country’s history. The significance of January 16 cannot be understood without revisiting the events of the country’s first military coup. In the early hours of January 15, 1966, a group of young military officers launched Nigeria’s first coup d’état. By the morning of January 16, the consequences of the coup were evident. Several of Nigeria’s most prominent political and military leaders had been assassinated. Among those killed were Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto and Premier of Northern Nigeria; Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Nigeria’s first Prime Minister; Brigadier Samuel Ademulegun; Brigadier Zakariya Maimalari; and other senior political and military figures. While leaders from different regions were affected, the perception in the North was that the coup disproportionately targeted Northern political leadership. This perception would profoundly shape political attitudes and inter-ethnic relations for decades. The events following the coup further deepened Northern grievances. Major General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi assumed power and suspended parts of the constitutional order. In many parts of Northern Nigeria, suspicion and anger grew rapidly, culminating in the counter-coup of July 1966. The resulting instability ultimately contributed to the chain of events that led to the Nigerian Civil War. More than six decades later, the memory of January 1966 remains alive. For many Northern families, historians, traditional institutions, and political observers, January 16 is not merely another date on the calendar. It is a reminder of a traumatic turning point that altered Nigeria’s political trajectory and claimed the lives of leaders who continue to be revered across the region. Against this backdrop, the decision to hold a presidential election on January 16 raises legitimate questions. Whether the date was chosen for logistical, constitutional, or electoral reasons, policymakers should recognize that symbolism matters in politics. Elections are national events meant to unite citizens around a shared democratic purpose. When an election coincides with a date associated with historical mourning for a significant section of the country, there is a risk that the symbolism overshadows the democratic exercise itself. nigeria.title: One dead, five injured in clash at Asaba political rally
nigeria.description: One person has been killed and five others injured in a violent clash during a political rally organised by the Obedient/OK Movement in support of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Asaba, Delta State. The incident occurred at about 12:15 p.m. on Saturday, 7 November 2026, along Nnebisi Road in Asaba. The identities of the victims are yet to be established. According to a statement by the Delta State Police Command, the police had received an intelligence report indicating the likelihood of violence and invited the organisers to a security meeting. “During the engagement, they were briefed on the identified security threats and advised against holding an open road procession. They were further encouraged to conduct their political activities at a designated venue where appropriate security will be provided for them. However, the organisers ignored this important security advice and proceeded with the road procession,” the statement said. Upon receiving a distress call, police operatives mobilised to the scene and took the injured victims to the hospital for medical attention. Security was subsequently reinforced in the affected area to forestall further breakdown of law and order, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. Commissioner of Police Samuel E. Erale condemned the violence and reiterated that political parties are free to conduct lawful campaigns and other political activities. “He, however, advises all political parties and their supporters to avoid road processions in the interest of public safety and to liaise with the Police ahead of any political gatherings to facilitate adequate security arrangements,” the statement said. The CP assured residents of Delta State of the Command’s commitment to a thorough and impartial investigation and urge anyone with useful information to contact the Command through the following phone numbers; 09155570008 or 09155570007. nigeria.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia to level Liga leaders Barca
nigeria.description: Kylian Mbappe scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia on Saturday. Reigning champions Barca visit Atletico Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack. Jose Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla stadium as they secured an eighth win in a row across all competitions. Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first half goals put Madrid in the driving seat and Mbappe added a third in the second half. Los Blancos were without winger Vinicius Junior, who was serving the final game of a four-match ban. Madrid have thrived in his absence, putting heavy pressure on Barca, whom they beat in the Camp Nou Clasico on October 25. In the ninth minutes the match stopped for players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who tragically died on Tuesday. Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a smart save to deny Aaron Mayol, who had picked Aurelien Tchouameni’s pocket in a dangerous area. Valencia’s Guido Rodriguez had a goal disallowed for offside before Mourinho’s side took control. Valverde drilled Madrid ahead from outside the area after Mbappe’s free-kick was blocked by the Valencia wall and fell to the Uruguayan. Guler soon doubled the lead, after Jude Bellingham’s cross was deflected kindly into his path. Guler had a good chance for the third in early in the second half but Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski grabbed the ball as the midfielder tried to round him. Minutes later Dimitrievski saved well from Mbappe as the French striker ran through and tried to dink the ball over him. Bellingham powered his way through the defence and was also denied by the goalkeeper, as was Mbappe following up with an overhead kick, as Madrid tried to find a third to kill off the game. Eventually Mbappe produced it, bursting onto a dangerous pass by Guler to dart past Dimitrievski and squeeze home his 13th league goal of the campaign. It was the forward’s 17th goal in 16 games across all competitions. Mbappe has netted in his last seven appearances for Madrid. Valencia’s Jose Gaya was dismissed with around 10 minutes remaining for a late sliding foul on Mbappe to further spoil Javier Aguirre’s team’s night. Earlier new Espanyol coach Eder Sarabia’s side were held to a goalless home draw by Deportivo La Coruna. Osasuna snatched a late 1-1 draw against Athletic Bilbao, while Racing Santander came from behind to beat Malaga 2-1. nigeria.title: Gas transportation network not responsible for power generation drop – NNPC
nigeria.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has said its gas transportation network remains available to supply gas to power generating stations nationwide, insisting that transportation constraints are not responsible for the current decline in electricity generation. The national oil company said operational records of its subsidiary, NNPC Gas Infrastructure Company Limited (NGIC), showed no transportation-related constraints within its network that could explain the drop in power generation. NNPC disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, in Abuja on Friday. The clarification followed a November 5 statement by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which attributed the decline in electricity generation partly to limited gas availability and reduced water inflows into hydroelectric power stations. However, NNPC said its clarification was specifically about the operational status of its gas transportation infrastructure, noting that gas production, commercial supply arrangements and actual deliveries to individual power plants were separate issues requiring independent assessment. The company said gas production had grown by about 10 per cent year-to-date in 2026, attributing the increase to the Federal Government’s gas development and monetisation agenda. “Gas supply availability is therefore not a challenge as NNPC remains committed to supporting efforts to improve electricity generation through safe, reliable and efficient gas supply and transportation,” the statement said. NNPC further explained that determining the causes of the generation shortfall required an assessment of other components of the gas-to-power value chain. These, it said, included the availability and operational readiness of generating units, plant maintenance schedules and actual gas offtake by power stations. The company stressed that the factors must be examined alongside gas supply data to establish the specific causes of the decline in electricity generation. It also called for a coordinated review of operational data by gas suppliers, transporters, power generators and NISO to identify constraints and guide appropriate interventions. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to developing dependable energy infrastructure and collaborating with stakeholders to translate the country’s gas resources into more reliable electricity supply for Nigerians. nigeria.title: Olawepo-Hashim visits Sowore, condemns political violence
nigeria.description: Former presidential candidate, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has condemned political violence in Nigeria, warning that attacks on political opponents could worsen the country’s already precarious security situation. Olawepo-Hashim also called on President Bola Tinubu to caution members of his team against actions and statements capable of provoking political conflict. He made the remarks in a statement posted on his X platform on Saturday after visiting activist and publisher, Omoyele Sowore, following the reported attack on him in Ekiti State. Olawepo-Hashim said his visit was motivated by their longstanding relationship, which dates back to their participation in the struggle against military dictatorship and the campaign for democracy. He warned that Nigeria, already grappling with terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security challenges, could not afford another crisis arising from political violence. “Nigeria cannot afford to add political violence to the general insecurity in the land. “Nigeria is already battling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and widespread insecurity. We cannot afford to add political violence to this burden,” he said. The former presidential candidate welcomed a statement by a United Nations representative expressing concern over the incident and urged other international partners to condemn political violence. He also urged political leaders to exercise restraint, warning that those who provoke violence might not be the ones to suffer its consequences. “President Bola Tinubu must call his team to order. Political leaders must exercise restraint and stop actions or rhetoric capable of provoking conflict. Those who recklessly provoke violence may not be the ones who bear its consequences,” he said. Recalling their history, Olawepo-Hashim said he and Sowore had been comrades since 1989/1990, when they worked together against military rule. He said he was particularly moved by Sowore’s recollection of how he introduced him to political activism at the University of Lagos. According to him, Sowore reaffirmed during the visit that he remained undeterred by the reported attack and was determined to continue campaigning for genuine democracy. Olawepo-Hashim stressed that political disagreements should not be used as justification for violence, urging Nigerians to uphold democratic values and reject actions capable of worsening insecurity and instability in the country. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. sports.title: Russell vents fury at Mercedes after missing out on pole in São Paulo
sports.description: FILE PHOTO - British formula One driver George Russell of team Mercedes speaks to the media at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, ahead of the Mexican Formula One Grand Prix. (is associated with: «Russell vents fury at Mercedes after missing out on pole in São Paulo») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa George Russell was again left furious with his Mercedes team after being pipped to pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix by Lando Norris. Norris, deposed as world champion by Kimi Antonelli last weekend, conquered thunderstorms to clinch an impressive pole as the rain poured down. Russell was facing a five-place grid penalty due to an engine change but was still determined to land pole as he and Norris slugged it out. But he was told to back off on his final flying lap before the rain worsened and his chance had gone. "You told me to back off, what the hell?" Russell bellowed on the radio. Team principal Toto Wolff tried to calm his driver by saying: "George, you are p2." That seemed to make matters worse, as Russell barked: "P2? I don't want to be P2, I want to be P1!" It adds to a season of frustration for pre-season title favourite Russell, having had to watch 20-year-old team-mate Antonelli storm to the title while he says he had been undone by issues in 14 of the 20 weekends prior to this. "Congrats to Lando but that was a pole lap and a misjudgement on our side," Russell said. "For me personally, given the circumstances of last week, it would have meant a lot to me to take pole today. "I missed it last week by nine milliseconds, but that was a real surprise. Today I really felt every lap I was doing was... I was at the top of the leaderboard most laps I completed. "So yeah, I'm really disappointed with how that panned out. In the scheme of things, it doesn't change a huge amount." Russell was asked about the message from Wolff but played down any frustration over it. "When you're a driver, you're the one who feels it the most," he added. "You've got to remember, we collectively made a misjudgement today. And there's members of my team who are going to be feeling as bad as I am currently. So it's important to remember that and we need to just keep the morale high. "There's no point for pole, but it would have just been a nice little one to add to the tally." Wolff admitted in a video posted by Mercedes they may have made the wrong call with Russell behind Alex Albon on track, saying: "George was absolutely the quickest and should have been on pole. We are trying to do our best, I'm not sure we should have aborted the lap." Russell will start seventh, one of a number of drivers hit by grid drops. Lewis Hamilton received a 10-place penalty but his new engine began smoking during practice and Ferrari ultimately had to change his entire power unit. Ashton Neally added two touchdowns for the Hawks, the first on a 19-yard reception of a Nate Bretch throw, and the second on a 4-yard run that put Corning up, 44-7, just over two minutes into the final quarter. "It wasn't like somebody ran for 200 yards," Johnston said. "It was a collective effort by our team. A lot of the credit goes to our line. We were able to throw the ball tonight as well, and our defense was pretty solid as well. Just an all-around great effort by everybody." Touchdowns for Ithaca (5-5) came on a 36-yard run from Jasmir Robbins in the first half, and a 29-yard strike from Leo Fiorello to Shy'von Williams late in the game. Robbins rushed for 72 yards on eight carries. He sat out the second half after he was shaken up on the final play of the first half. Corning responded after a 33-7 loss to Union-Endicott in last week's regular-season finale. Little went right for the Hawks in that game, including more than 200 penalty yards, a dropped touchdown, and some injuries that sidelined key players in the second half. "I'd like to think that we turned the corner," Johnston said. "We've still got a ways to go with some guys, getting them healthy. I know Elmira gets the bye week and their kids will be back to full go." Up next : Corning (6-4) will play Elmira (6-3) in the championship game at 6 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13 at Elmira's Thomas J. Hurley Athletic Complex. Elmira topped Corning, 14-8, in the regular season and has beaten the Hawks in the last three Section 4 Class AA finals.

sports.title: 5 major takeaways from Penn State’s nail-biting win over Washington
sports.description: It feels like Penn State has finally regained control over its season. After a four-game losing streak that followed a 3-0 start to the season, the blue and white have won two in a row, and it looks like they truly belong in the Big Ten. The Nittany Lions took on Washington on Saturday afternoon, and they won 28-25 in what was almost a mirror image of the Wisconsin game earlier in the season. The offense moved the ball and scored at will in the first half, while the defense put a familiar beatdown on the Huskies ’ offense. But then the offense went cold in the final two quarters, and the defense softened up and allowed the Huskies back in the game. However, Penn State was able to salt away the game in the end, and it escaped Washington with a win. Here are five of the biggest takeaways from the team’s second conference win of the season. We belong For a while there, it looked like head coach Matt Campbell and his gang of Iowa State transfers were no match for the Big Ten. They lost their first four games in the conference, and they were getting out-coached and outplayed for much of that time. But after back-to-back wins, with those Cyclones players being the focal points, their viability in the conference is no longer in question. There may not be much to accomplish for the team this season, but this is solid groundwork for the development of the program going forward. Beggars can’t be choosers Washington might not be the cream of the crop in the Big Ten, but they are certainly a good team. Penn State’s fans have been starving for a win against a team that has some life, and they finally got it this week. If may not have been the prettiest game, and the Nittany Lions may have avoided a catastrophe at the end of the game, but a win is a win. A victory was what everyone wanted, so we can’t complain about the path it took to get here. Competition It looked like Koby Howard was Penn State’s clear-cut best wide receiver when the season began. Now that he’s been out of action for more than two months, we’re finding out that it may not be the case. Wide receiver Chase Sowell has thrived in Howard’s absence, and he had the best game of his career by far on Saturday. He finished the contest with four catches for 125 yards and a touchdown, and he had a number of highlight plays that made him look like a star. Not only is it looking like the Nittany Lions have two No. 1 receivers, but they might both be stars as well. Rookie wall Linebacker Josiah Zayas struggled mightily for the first time all season. The true freshman got juked out on the very first play from scrimmage, and it set the table for the rest of the game. The Huskies tried to make a late push, and on the touchdown they scored to make the game 28-17, Zayas seemed confused about what he was supposed to be doing in coverage. He then gave up another touchdown on a fourth-quarter drive where he slipped. He looks like he has a bright future on this team, but Saturday’s game was not a good one for him

sports.title: 3 quick takeaways from Badgers win over Rutgers: The Ryan Hopkins era is here
sports.description: MADISON, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 07: Ryan Hopkins #10 of the Wisconsin Badgers takes off running in the second quarter against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Camp Randall Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers blew out the Rutgers Scarlet Knights 31-10 on Saturday, earning bowl eligibility for the first time in three years as they improved to 6-2 on the season. True freshman Ryan Hopkins got his first career start, while the Badgers had another offensive line change. Still, they got out ahead early and finished the game strong en route to a blowout. Here are three quick takeaways from Wisconsin’s win over Rutgers. Hopkins has his moments For one of the first times this season, we saw the Badgers passing attack see some life. Yes, it was against a poor Rutgers team that didn’t have much pressure, but Hopkins looked fairly confident in the pocket and the Badgers let him rip. Hopkins made a number of good plays, as well as a few he would want back that didn’t end up hurting the Badgers. But he looked the part as a true freshman. He was very efficient throwing the ball, looked to target all parts of the field, and made throws that Colton Joseph hadn’t made. Wisconsin now gets a trial period with Hopkins over the next three games to assess where he’s at ahead of the 2027 season. But it was a very positive look in his first start. Pressuring the quarterback The Badgers came to play defensively, and a big part of it was getting after the quarterback. Wisconsin had five sacks, with Sebastian Cheeks, Nicolas Clayton, Charles Perkins, Nolan Vils, and Junior Poyser all getting sacks. They were able to pressure AJ Surace quite a bit, and stopping the run helped them get into third down situations, where they held Rutgers to 4 of 13 on third downs. It was a better day after Wisconsin couldn’t disrupt the quarterback against Iowa, with Hank Brown completing 20 of 24 passes for 222 yards. Good day for the boys up front. Bowl eligible It should be the expectation, but Wisconsin has returned to bowl eligibility after two disappointing years. It was a good bounce back for the Badgers, who were embarrassed last weekend, as they dominated Rutgers for much of this one. Now, the focus should be on Wisconsin winning at least two or the next three to take advantage of their favorable schedule. Going forward, the focus needs to be on Ryan Hopkins’s development and continued improvement of the offense, while Wisconsin’s defense remains to be aggressive. With how Wisconsin looked on Saturday, it feels like they must win that season-ender against Minnesota to cap off a successful season. But they had a strong performance Saturday and reached a key milestone.

sports.title: Rutgers Offense Stalls in Second Half, Falls to Wisconsin 31 to 10
sports.description: MADISON, WI - NOVEMBER 07: Rutgers Scarlet Knights quarterback AJ Surace (10) throws a pass in a college football game between the Rutgers Scarlet Knights and the Wisconsin Badgers on November 7th, 2026 at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, WI. (Photo by Dan Sanger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Rutgers football fell to Wisconsin 31 to 10 in a game where a three-point halftime deficit turned into a rout by the game’s end. In the final 30 minutes of play, the Scarlet Knights would be held scoreless while the Badgers found the momentum offensively to pull away. Rutgers would keep it close throughout the first half, as they only found themselves down by three at halftime. The Knights would force the Badgers to punt twice and would twice strand the Badgers on fourth down deep in their own territory twice, forcing them to take two field goals. Rutgers would keep pace by scoring a touchdown of their own, off of a 30-yard touchdown pass to freshman wide receiver Dyzier Carter, and by hitting a 45-yard field goal. The field goal was kicked by Jack Scullion, with starting kicker Dane Pizarro out due to injury. Wisconsin’s offense would start humming in the second half, with the Knights having no answer for it. The Badgers would kick a field goal on their first drive of the half to extend their lead before scoring two touchdowns on their next two drives. Rutgers’ defense would recover a fumble on Wisconsin’s fourth drive of the half, but their offense would be unable to score for the entire half as the Badgers would cruise to victory. The Knights’ defense continued the tradition of making backup freshman quarterbacks look like battle-tested veterans, as they allowed Ryan Hopkins to complete 18 out of 24 passes for 241 yards and three touchdowns. On the ground, Wisconsin ran the ball 29 times for 122 yards. On offense, the Knights struggled to keep their quarterback upright, as they surrendered five total sacks on the day and eight total tackles for loss. They also struggled to get the run going, totaling 94 yards on 36 carries, or 2.6 yards per carry. The one slight positive in this game is that AJ Surace looked more consistent in this game than in games past. He completed 14 out of 24 total passes for 161 yards, one touchdown, and no interceptions. This game was a step in the right direction for Surace, compared to his performance in games past. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land. science.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
science.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere. It's high and well placed during the evening, and this week the moon is becoming particularly cooperative. New Moon falls around Nov. 9, giving us several evenings with little or no moonlight to wash out faint deep-sky objects. I usually begin with the star Alpheratz, one of the corner stars of the Great Square of Pegasus. You go two stars left, two stars up, and you arrive at M31. Another route — and a good way to check you're in the right place — starts in Cassiopeia, the distinctive W-shaped constellation high in the northeastern sky on autumn evenings. You can use its second V-shape as an arrow pointing straight at M31. You can do that star-hop with the naked eye or a pair of binoculars, but M31 is visible to the naked eye only under a very dark sky. However, don't look for a miniature version of the photographs. Expect a faint, elongated patch with a slightly brighter middle. There's another beginner trap to avoid. Images make Andromeda look compact, but its full apparent extent is enormous — several times the width of the full moon — and our eyes usually pick up only the much brighter central region. science.title: Giant exoplanet emerges from the dark when the James Webb Space Telescope turns out the starlight
science.description: null Sometimes science can seem really counter-intuitive. For example, occasionally in astronomy, you can see more with less light. Case in point: the emergence of a giant planet in observations made by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), when astronomers found a way to block out light from the planet's parent star. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , in question is 51 Eridani b (51 ERI b), a gas giant with the same mass as around 11 Jupiters that orbits a star located around 97 light-years away. 51 ERI b was discovered back in 2015 by ground-based telescopes, but the planet was missing from observations of the system made by the JWST. That wasn't a failing of the JWST itself; no one is doubting the observing capabilities of the most powerful telescope humanity has ever hoisted into orbit around Earth. Instead, it was a result of starlight from the star 51 ERI A obscuring this intimidatingly massive world. The brightest planets are 100,000 times fainter than their host stars, meaning spotting them is like observing a firefly hovering around a lighthouse. Even using a tool called a coronagraph to block the star isn't enough to reveal the planet, as that doesn't stop all the starlight. The only solution to this glaring problem is a computer program to wipe out the starlight. "For the past 20 years, astronomers have tackled this problem by observing a different star and using its image as a reference," Jason Wang of Northwestern University explained in a statement . "Then, they subtract that reference image from the original observation to remove the unwanted glare to reveal faint planets that otherwise might be hidden." There is a problem with this process, however. Even the most stable telescopes "wobble." For instance, the JWST requires cryocoolers to keep its NIRCam instrument super cold, and those coolers have little motors that can cause the mirrors to vibrate. This movement, however slight, causes a scatter in starlight. The result is enough glare remaining to obscure a planet, but Wang and colleagues developed a new approach to this problem. Telescopes their more stable digital twins The new approach taken by the team is dubbed Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), and it involves creating a digital "twin" of a telescope. Essentially a virtual replica that simulates how starlight travels through the telescope's mirrors and reaches its detectors. This twin is then fine-tuned to account for millions of tiny imperfections in the original telescope. The digital twin is then tweaked until it aligns with observations from the actual telescope. Astronomers can then remove the simulated glare from the original image. To assess the validity of the technique, the researchers took a second look at JWST observations of two star systems with known exoplanets, HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani , and one system, TYC 5899, with no known planets.
